Football: A Speculative Future History

2015 - 2025

Our trip begins with what became known as the Historic Era Football. This was a single nation, eleven on eleven football league made up of two conferences, each having 16 teams split into four divisions. The annual champions were decided by a playoff system resulting in the best team from each conference playing one Super Bowl game. One bureaucratic league created and controlled by the collective of team owners oversaw the impartial functions of running a fair and competitive sport. Alternate rules professional football existed elsewhere in the world, but was not as widely popular.

2025 - 2040

Early implementation of international teams with Toronto, Mexico City, Havana, and London fielding teams in the 2025-26 season. Expansion of the league to 40 teams allowed each division to gain a new team and each conference two international teams. The playoff system was expanded, but the result was still decided by the best team from each conference playing one Super Bowl game. The league granted exclusivity deals for all facets of global distribution beginning the adoption of the colloquially used term 'Worlds Favourite Pastime'.

2040 - 2060

The league, ever conscious of it's image, re-branded itself as the Global Football League. The two conferences were renamed and Western and Eastern based on their respective global hemisphere, though all divisions continued using directional names generally representative of their locations. After some league sponsored/bullied relocations, more international teams in geographically convenient locations formed a new global network of control. Some alternate rules leagues competed for relevance, but none were able to internationalize as completely as had the Americans.

2060-2068

With colonization of Luna well established, and the complications of settling Mars smoothing out, The faltering Canadian and Australian Football leagues combined to form the Lunar Football League. Drafting new rules based both on the combination of the two styles of play as well as on the unique properties of lunar gravity, the league began play with 16 teams divided into two divisions. These teams played ten games during the Terran off-season and the top four played off with the winners facing off in one Lunar Bowl game. Initially surprised by the formation, the GFL at first renounced the sport as a completely different, and later lobbied Terran governments to ban transmission of the sport.

2068-2072

Though some blackout rules were created against lunar broadcasting they were never widely enforced. While some areas of the world, particularly the American south and the middle east, forbade the broadcast, others completely embraced the new league. This gave legitimacy to the league, and encouraged another league on Mars to follow their example. This league, having only ten teams playing a form of eight on eight to start with barely survived past the initial few years.

2072 -2075

In another bold move, the GFL launched alternatives to both the struggling LFL and the floundering MFL, adopting the eleven on eleven lunar rules directly, and only changing the eight person martian rules slightly. Though the two smaller leagues could not boast the same return on investment, they remained respectfully high in viewer ratings. Initially proposed as a competition killer, these new leagues (branded as GFL Solar) had the opposite effect. By increasing both awareness of and legitimacy to the two financially strapped leagues the GFL measured the only overall change to be a sharp drop in standard GFL viewer percentages.

2075 - 2093

Vying for relevance in an expanding market, the GFL agrees to partially merge with the LFL's newly proposed Solar Football League. The GFL would retain the Terran sport entirely, and gain control of all MFL operations as well as the newly created martian-rules league on Venus (MFL2). The LFL would take over the new lunar-rules league on Enceladus. The resulting championships would take place before the start of the next sport season dividing the solar calendar roughly into thirds for most of the football loving human population beginning to spread throughout the solar system.

2093 -2105

SFL operations continued uninterrupted for almost 20 seasons before the great solar war halted sports and entertainment throughout the entire system. When the dust settled after the war in 2104, the populace was eager to get their minds off of fighting and onto something else. The SFL was there to oblige. All across the solar system the children of soldiers were graduating colleges and signing up for the SFL draft. Many of this wave became the first hall of famers not involved in the creation of the league. With the 2104 season only able to be played by the martian teams, the first full resumption of all solar football was in the 2105 season.

2105 - 2117

After the war, economic revolution lead to many advancements which had been stymied by the previous system. One such advancement was basic interstellar travel, and many of the resulting pilgrims took their love of football with them. Throughout the local parts of the galaxy leagues with variant rules sprung up and some flourished. While this had little immediate affect on the SFL, it would set the stage for wider football expansion.

2117 -

When hyper-spatial communication became viable, one of the first transmissions to the outlying stellar colonies was that years Lunar Bowl. As that technology became cheaper and easier, all three SFL seasons became annual draws from all parts of the civilized galaxy. And as human civilization spread ever farther out from the home system, so too did its sport, especially football.
